title: Performance panel, activity board and resource counters
objective: Show the editor's own memory, CPU and GPU use with one-minute sparklines and the long-running work in progress in a Performance section at the bottom of the state panel, backed by a host activity board and process resource counters that API clients read through activity.list and resources.read.
context_summary: The desktop has no view of its own resource use and nothing reports work in progress beyond job.status for source and analysis jobs. The design adds a per-owner activity board that workers publish to through a guard and clients read as a snapshot, so the panel and the publishers never know each other; a leaf crate with the platform counters (macOS footprint, CPU time, IORegistry GPU time and Metal allocations; Linux and Windows CPU and memory); widgets for sparkline metric rows and job rows; and a section that samples once a second only while expanded.

tasks.description: Add the lightwell-process crate with the platform process counters and the process-wide lightwell_core::resources sampler behind the resources.read method, including the colour-scratch and spatial budgets and declare_gpu_presenter.
extra_context: macOS GPU facts measured on 2026-09-23: task_power_info_v2 GPU utilisation is always 0 on Apple silicon; IOAccelerator child user clients carry AppUsage accumulatedGPUTime in nanoseconds keyed by IOUserClientCreator 'pid N, name'; walking them costs 0.35 ms p50, so cache this pid's entries.
The workspace forbids unsafe code; the new crate overrides that exactly as lightwell-raw does and adds no crate absent from Cargo.lock.

context_links.label: Performance panel design
context_links.relevance: Counter table, resources.read JSON contract and unavailable reporting.

context_links.label: Method table
context_links.relevance: Where resources.read is declared with its notes and handler.

context_links.label: Render budgets
context_links.relevance: ScratchBudget target, in-use and peak read into the budgets object.

acceptance_criteria: resources.read answers the documented shape with no parameters and no asset, is listed by schema.list, emits no event and reports each unavailable counter with a reason instead of a number.
On macOS CPU time, footprint, peak, resident memory and GPU time are real counters; GPU allocations are read only after declare_gpu_presenter and are unavailable with a reason otherwise.
Linux and Windows implementations of CPU time and memory compile; no native run is claimed.

steps: Unit tests: CPU time grows by at least 150 ms after a 200 ms spin; memory grows by at least 48 MiB after touching 64 MiB; peak is at least current.
macOS test: a Metal dispatch raises GPU time; allocations are unavailable before declare_gpu_presenter and a number after.
API test through the method table: shape, no event, schema listing.
expected_results: All tests pass and cargo xtask check passes.

tasks.description: Add the per-owner activity board with activity.list, publish source preparation, RAW redevelopment, preview jobs and owner-side analysis to it, and hand the desktop's preview queue the owner's board.
extra_context: The board holds state, not a stream: the event log stays a record of catalog mutations and gains nothing.
Guards finish on drop as cancelled, or failed while panicking; 64 active entries with an untracked count past that; 16 recent entries of work that ran at least 250 ms.

context_links.label: Performance panel design
context_links.relevance: Board API, bounds, publishers table and activity.list contract.

context_links.label: Catalog owner
context_links.relevance: Source worker, analysis completion and OwnerHandle::start_with.

context_links.label: Preview queue
context_links.relevance: The job thread that publishes preview.render with its proxy and exact phases.

acceptance_criteria: activity.list answers the documented shape, is listed by schema.list, needs no asset and emits no event.
Each listed publisher appears while running and, when it ran at least 250 ms, in recent afterwards with its outcome; a superseded preview's exact phase finishes as cancelled.
Exposure drag input-to-frame on 24 MP is unchanged within host noise when measured before and after.

steps: Board unit tests for every rule in the design's acceptance list.
Owner tests with a test gate that holds a source preparation and an analysis job running while activity.list is read.
Preview queue test that a job reports proxy then exact and ends when the queue releases it.
expected_results: All tests pass and cargo xtask check passes.

tasks.description: Build the Performance section in the desktop: the view model with rates, formatters, scales and job display rules, the pinned layout under the state panel's scrollable, the gated one-second sampler, evidence state and step, and the performance smoke scenario.
extra_context: The timer exists only while the section is expanded and the state panel is shown; collapsed, the section makes no request.

acceptance_criteria: The section matches the design's layout on the M4 in the performance scenario's captures, with correlated state for every frame.

The scenario checks the displayed text against the recorded samples, the rates against the counters, the job rows against activity.list, no samples while collapsed, and memory against the runner's own reading of the process.

steps: View-model unit tests; subscription gating test; the performance smoke scenario on the M4.
commands: cargo run --release --package xtask -- smoke --scenario performance --output artifacts/performance
expected_results: Tests and the scenario pass; captures inspected.
